summary: The Magdalen friendship Wilde's teasing letter to Boulton gives away: 'whom by the bye I believe you like much better than yours truly.' The editors identify 'Sir John' as most probably Sir John Alexander Hanham, Magdalen undergraduate 1875-8.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote: Will you come and see me tonight at nine o'clock or any time when you can escape from 'Sir John' - whom by the bye I believe you like _much better_ than yours truly
sources.context: Wilde to Harold Boulton, [? April 1878], Magdalen College (MS Yale). 'much better' is underlined in the original. The editors identify 'Sir John' as most probably Sir John Alexander Hanham, ninth Baronet, Magdalen undergraduate 1875-8. He is the rival in the only letter that carries `boulton--wilde`.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Boulton had a preferred companion, and who the editors think he was.
